related_questions.question: How quickly can you take a COVID test after exposure?

text_blocks.snippet: If you develop symptoms of COVID-19, test immediately. If you don't have symptoms, it's recommended to wait at least 5 full days after your last exposure before testing. If your initial test is negative, but you continue to have symptoms or were exposed to COVID-19, retest as directed.
snippet_highlighted_words: If you develop symptoms of COVID-19, test immediately.
If you don't have symptoms, it's recommended to wait at least 5 full days after your last exposure before testing

list.title: Symptomatic Individuals:
list.snippet: If you experience symptoms of COVID-19, such as fever, cough, or fatigue, get tested as soon as possible.

list.title: Asymptomatic Individuals:
list.snippet: If you don't have symptoms but were exposed, wait at least 5 full days after your exposure before taking a test.

list.title: Retesting:
list.snippet: If your initial test is negative, but you still have symptoms or were exposed, retest as instructed, as it can take a few days for the virus to be detectable by some tests.

list.title: Contagiousness:
list.snippet: Even if you test negative, you could still be contagious, especially if you test too early after exposure.
